questions.stem: An architect elicits 3 hoped-for and 2 feared selves; what is the total number of possible selves?
questions.explanation: 3 plus 2 equals 5 possible selves. Direct addition.

questions.topic: Personality: What a Self-Efficacy Claim Is About
questions.stem: An architect rates self-efficacy 7 of 10; what percent of maximum is that?
questions.explanation: 7 of 10 is 70 percent. Direct conversion.

questions.topic: Personality: Beliefs About Capability Against What People Did
questions.stem: An architect finds efficacy 8 and performance 6 on 10-point scales; what is the gap?
questions.explanation: 8 minus 6 equals 2 points. Direct subtraction.

questions.topic: Personality: A Comment That Is Taken Well and One That Is Not
questions.stem: An architect finds 70 percent take a comment well and 30 percent do not; what is the ratio?
questions.explanation: 70 divided by 30 equals 2.3333. Direct division.

questions.topic: Personality: A Criterion Figure That Is Easy to Misread
questions.stem: An architect reads r = 0.40 between trait and criterion; what percent of variance is explained?
questions.explanation: 0.40 squared is 0.16, or 16 percent. Squaring gives explained variance.
